author: CocoNeedsHelp
text_post: I have olive skin and jet black hair. I don't think you will have a problem though; I think the reason why laser hair removal wasn't as effective on me was because of my hormonal imbalances. At this point, i think my hair follicles are fried from how much i have lasered them xD but because of my hormonal imbalance and hirsutism (a condition that literally means my body hair grows way too fast and thick) the laser has been rendered useless on most parts of my body; with the exception of my armpits and my bikini area. For some reason, the hair on those areas have permanently disappeared.  It's most probably because the hair on our face, armpits and pubes are terminal hair, whereas the hair on the rest of our body identifies as vellus. They function differently and aren't that correlated at all, which may explain the laser reacted differently to them.  My advice for you doing laser is: 1. Shave your hair 1-2 days beforehand. Some dermatologists will tell you to shave 3-4 days prior, but at that point your hair has already progressed in the growth cycle and the laser won't work as well (this is a trick used by dermatologists to drain their clients from money).  2. Exfoliate 5 days after lasering, this removes dead skin cells and prevents any in grown hairs.  3. When you finally do the actual laser, make sure your skin doesn't have any products on it. Any make-up, deodorant etc will literally burn your skin xd. I recommend using baby wipes rather than deodorant on the day you laser.  I wish you the best of luck
